title: The Restorer's Dilemma
summary: A conservator hired to clean a village mural finds an older painting hidden beneath it and must decide what to preserve.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: Ama on a small scaffold in a village hall, gently cleaning a faded mural with a soft brush, a hidden blue sky showing beneath, no text

chapters.title: A Routine Commission
sentences: The village council hired Ama to restore a mural that had decorated the town hall for nearly a century.
It showed a harvest festival, but the colours had faded so badly that the farmers looked like grey ghosts.
She expected a routine job of a few weeks, involving careful cleaning and a little repair.
On the first morning she tested a small corner with a damp cotton swab, working slowly because the plaster was fragile.
Gradually, the dull surface lifted to reveal a patch of unexpected blue beneath the dirt.
It was far too bright to belong to the harvest scene above it.
Ama paused, leaned closer, and noticed the faint outline of a sailing ship.
She realised that another painting lay underneath, and that someone had deliberately covered it.
For a long moment she simply stood there, unsure whether she had found a treasure or a problem.

chapters.title: What the Archives Said
sentences: That evening Ama visited the village archive, where an elderly clerk brought her a box of yellowing documentation.
The records showed that the first mural, a seascape, had been painted by a local fisherman's daughter.
It had been covered after only a year, following a long argument about whether the hall should display a seascape at all.
The mayor at the time had wanted something cheerful, and the sea reminded many families of those who never came home.
Ama felt a quiet sympathy for both sides of that old controversy.
The clerk seemed reluctant to say more, but she finally admitted that the painter's name had been scratched from every register.
Ama thought that erasing a name was a harsher way to conceal the past than erasing a picture.
She returned to the hall at dawn, determined to learn how much of the seascape had survived.
Under the lamp, the hidden ship looked like it was still sailing, undamaged by a hundred years of silence.

chapters.title: Two Pictures, One Wall
sentences: Ama knew that she could not preserve both paintings in the way the council had imagined.
Removing the harvest scene would destroy a work that generations of villagers had grown to love.
Leaving the seascape hidden, however, would continue a silence that had lasted far too long.
After several sleepless nights she proposed a compromise: she would carefully open a narrow window in the upper layer.
Through it, visitors could glimpse the ship while the harvest scene remained largely intact.
A small plaque would honour the original painter by name, restoring what the old registers had taken away.
At the evening when the council came to unveil the result, the hall was unusually quiet.
An old woman, the painter's great-granddaughter, stood at the front and whispered her gratitude.
Ama understood then that the village's heritage was not a single picture, but a legacy made of two difficult stories.
